A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ModPrompt research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support matching content across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection experiments on LLVIP, FLIR, and NYUv2, including prompt ablations, text-residual experiments, larger-backbone evaluations, and qualitative detections.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical evaluations and adds a YOLO-World comparison of LLVIP performance, COCO knowledge preservation, and trainable parameter counts.

M1.justification: Both versions train an image-conditioned encoder-decoder prompt and additive residuals on frozen text embeddings using the same objectives. MPDR renames and elaborates the earlier task-residual mechanism. The decoder constraints and residual zero-masking are newly documented details, without evidence of an actual procedural revision.

E1.justification: V2 Table 4 adds evaluation on COCO to test preservation of RGB-domain detection knowledge. LLVIP infrared, FLIR infrared, and NYUv2 depth coverage remains; moving FLIR results into the appendix does not remove that coverage.

E2.justification: The standalone Task Residuals comparator in v1 Tables 4 and 5 disappears from the corresponding v2 Tables 2 and 7 for both detectors across all three modality datasets. Combined visual-prompt/residual methods remain under MPDR terminology, and the other principal comparator families are retained.

E3.justification: V2 Table 4 introduces joint LLVIP/COCO evaluation using AP50 and an average across the two datasets. Existing modality-dataset splits, detector variants, training budgets, and AP metrics remain unchanged. The new comparison does not fully specify its COCO split or configuration.

E4.justification: V2 adds a dedicated catastrophic-forgetting and parameter-efficiency analysis in Table 4. Conversely, removing the residual-only rows reduces the component-ablation evidence. Existing prompt-size, translator-backbone, larger-detector, and qualitative analyses are retained, often in different locations.

E5.justification: V1 Table 3 reports uncertainty values for HalluciDet and ModTr. Its replacements, v2 main Figure 4 and supplementary Figure 2, show bars without uncertainty. Other tables largely retain their ± reporting, and neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: Most matched benchmark values are unchanged. V2 Table 4 adds COCO AP50 results of 51.90 for ModPrompt, 0.66 for head finetuning, and 0.10 for full finetuning; residual-only results are removed. Section 8.5 newly claims superiority on every FLIR AP metric, although its plot retains ModTr's AP50 advantage, reported in v1 as 69.20 versus 69.03.

T1.justification: The detection definitions and objectives in Equations 1–5, including the appendix text-prompt formulation, remain mathematically unchanged. V2 adds explanatory prose but no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim backbone-agnostic modality adaptation, preservation of zero-shot knowledge, superiority over conventional pixel prompts, and performance sometimes comparable to full finetuning. MPDR terminology makes the existing text-residual contribution more explicit without materially changing these central claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains recovery of original text embeddings by zero-masking residuals and adds explicit limitations concerning target-label dependence, introduced noise, and duplicate detections. Existing small-object limitations remain. However, it removes v1's explicit qualification that offline vocabulary adaptation produces a closed-vocabulary detector.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents pretrained encoder initialization, three decoder output channels bounded between zero and one, residual zero-masking, and trainable parameter counts. Existing optimization, hardware, and code-access information remains. V1's disclosure that HalluciDet and ModTr use Faster R-CNN is removed.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Bansal et al.'s Zero-Shot Object Detection and DINO, while removing CORA, DetCLIP, Faster R-CNN, and Dive into Deep Learning. It refines the contrast with classification-oriented task residuals and traditional modality translators, while retaining the principal research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction is substantially rewritten and reordered, the method explanation expands, and the residual discussion is renamed MPDR. Results are reorganized around LLVIP/NYUv2 in the main text and FLIR in the supplement, whose results subsections are extensively restructured and followed by a dedicated limitations section.

P2.justification: Tables are split and recombined across the main text and appendix, the translator-comparison table becomes two bar-chart figures, and a new retention/parameter table is added. Figures 2 and 3 are redrawn to show residual addition explicitly. The qualitative image content is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 adds direct empirical support for the existing knowledge-preservation claim through the COCO comparison, while decoder details and explicit limitations improve transparency. These gains are limited by the removal of residual-only controls and translator uncertainty values, incomplete documentation of the new evaluation, and the incorrect claim of superiority on every FLIR metric. With the core method and benchmark performance largely unchanged, the net improvement is modest.
